Replay

Presenting Replay state

Read simulation frames and match recorded events across corrections while keeping display state separate.

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Frames and posesEvent journal

Use Replay's presentation helpers to draw copied simulation state and reconcile effects after correction. Simulation state stays in replay.Timeline; presentation reads detached frames and owns its own smoothing, scene nodes and effect state.

Frames and poses#

frames_at(&timeline, lower_tick, alpha) copies two adjacent frames. A missing lower frame is an explicit failure; sampling the current head holds that frame without extrapolation. Use the lower frame's entity membership/discrete state until the presentation clock reaches the next tick. Extract poses and pass them through pose_blend; a teleport explicitly selects the destination pose.

Smoother2 and Smoother3 carry position and angular correction error. Use smooth_correct_pose / smooth3_correct_pose for same-tick corrections, then present each render frame; ordinary motion continues while the error decays. Large discontinuities clear the smoothing error, snapping the displayed pose to the corrected state. Angular smoothing documents shortest arcs, quaternion composition, finite-input handling and Godot integration.

Event journal#

Odin
journal: view.Journal(Event)
err := view.journal_init(&journal, epoch = epoch, baseline = checkpoint_tick)
// Optional: view.journal_set_policy(&journal, classify_event)
// For every complete tick batch (empty ticks included):
err = view.sync_tick(&journal, tick, occurrences)
err = view.advance_time(&journal, confirmed_tick, watched_tick)
count := view.drain(&journal, changes[:])

An occurrence is a recorded gameplay event with an identity used to match it across replay. Its payload holds game-specific data; its identity lets the journal update, confirm or cancel the same effect. Each new occurrence receives a policy. Existing IDs keep their policy:

Policy When it begins
Speculative (default) On first observation; later changes may update/cancel it
Confirmed When the authority or peer-commit protocol settles its tick
Watched When confirmed and the visible cause's watch clock reaches its tick

Drain notifications outside simulation:

  • Begin: start the effect. confirmed distinguishes an already final occurrence.
  • Update: adjust an existing speculative effect; previous carries its old payload.
  • Cancel: remove or stop an effect whose occurrence disappeared during replay.
  • Confirm: an already begun speculative occurrence has become final; do not begin it again.

Payloads are stored by value, independent of live entity pointers. An impact or death effect can still begin after its source entity is destroyed. Put the required pose/details in its payload.

The journal has bounded tick/event history and a bounded output queue. Each sync_tick or advance_time is atomic with respect to tracked events and output. On Output_Full, drain and retry. It will not evict unconfirmed events or pending watched effects to make room. Capacity/history errors require backpressure or an explicit presentation reset/resync; do not silently drop them.

Synchronize complete batches through a frontier before confirming them. Once confirmed, batch membership and payloads cannot change. advance_time is monotonic within an epoch. To inspect an older committed playback, use a fresh epoch and explicitly tear down old effects/views. Rejoin initialization sets a baseline so historical one-shots cannot replay as new occurrences.

A newer checkpoint in the same epoch uses journal_rebase(&journal, tick). It retains already queued output, matures effects from previously confirmed batches at the new visible baseline, and cancels abandoned speculative effects. Already final effects do not begin again. Unconfirmed occurrences and missing batches in the gap do not become confirmed merely because a newer checkpoint exists. The new baseline must be at least the old confirmed and watched ticks.

Rebase is atomic. journal_rebase_check lets a runner check queue capacity before resetting its simulation timeline; the journal must stay unchanged between that check and commit. Output_Full requires draining and retrying. Capacity means the required notifications cannot fit even in an empty queue. A new epoch still uses journal_reset, with its separate old-scope cancellation contract.

replay.confirm_through separately protects the simulation frontier. A runner must establish that the ticks are settled under its authority or peer-commit protocol before calling it. Neither counter elects a host, authenticates packets, or guarantees durable external effects; those belong to the network/session authority contract and any application outbox or external service.

One_Shots retains consumed event IDs independently of active effects. It prevents an already heard one-shot from replaying when a cancelled occurrence reappears. Retirement is explicit and monotonic; retired IDs remain expired after their ring slots are reused. See the Godot audio adapter for the consumer contract, bounded capacities and voice-reuse behavior.

Visual cues turn journal changes into bounded, detached render instances with correction, cancellation, expiry and consumed-ID retention. Cavecrawl uses them for its event-backed combat bursts and hit flashes.

Bounded tick phases and linear previews support render-frame motion without stepping simulation or wrapping backward during prediction stalls.
